title: Bound on retained-state length
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $C,e$ be natural numbers, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Suppose $N,L$ are natural numbers with $|x|\le L$ and $N\le L$. For every $j\le N$, the retained state obtained after $j$ iterations of the producer step from the state encoding $x$, time zero, and an empty table has length at most $(8+8k)(L+1)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite-state binary Turing machine M with k work tapes
Natural number j with j ≤ N
replaced: For every source machine, parameters, instance $x$ of length at most $L$, and horizon $N \le L$, every iterate up to $N$ of the producer step from the empty retained state has length at most $(8 + 8k)(L+1)^2$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes.
